chapter: Philadelphia, New York and Sam Wooding in Europe
title: Lou Henry, Tim Brymn and a few dates with Chick Webb in New York
summary: Tickets from trombonist Lou Henry brought him to New York, then he worked with Tim Brymn and Chick Webb before Sam Wooding offered a trip to Europe.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I see. Now when you were with Bobby Lee and you -- you worked with Wilbur and around -- somewhere around 1928, didn't you play briefly with Chick Webb?

Well you see -- yes, now when I left for -- left Wilbur, there was a fellow in New York named [Lou] Henry, he was a trombone player. He sent couple of tickets to Philadelphia, to get us out of there. Cause we didn't have any money.

And we came to New York and joined Lou Henry's band. He put us up there in his apartment on 135th Street, between Seventh and Eighth Avenues. And he got us one room with the landlady there and we worked with Lou Henry. He had a little band around here. He was playing mostly theaters, with acts.

Then, that didn't last too long, then a fellow named Lt. Tim Brymn Brown, who came back from Europe or somewhere, he was -- had a little band, a stage band and which he directed and we went to work for Lt. Tim Brymn Brown. For awhile. He had a lot of the shows and singers and things. And that didn't -- that's where Sam Wooding came in and during --
Yes, because Sam had been with
Yes, but before Sam Wooding, I did work with Chick Webb's band. That's where I first met Johnny Hodges, and Freddy Jenkins. Well he was playing, like, dances.

You know, he play down to the hotel or some ballroom down there and I only played with him a couple of times. But he was just getting together and then that's when Sam Wooding came in and offered to take us to Europe. So I left Chick Webb and went right straight to Sam Wooding.
I see, well did anyone else leave Chick Webb with you for Sam Wooding?
Yes we were together all the time up until -- until after Sam Wooding, then he went with Lionel Hampton and I went with Cab.
